project.name: ree-v3
project.description: Active V3 implementation substrate for the REE cognitive-architecture research program, written in Python on PyTorch and NumPy. This scan is scoped to the two executable-code planes: ree_core/ (brain-region-named cognitive modules such as amygdala, PFC, hippocampal, sleep, cingulate, PAG, neuromodulation, basal-ganglia action-learning, affect and residue) and coordinator/ (a stdlib http.server coordination service with SQLite storage, a sync daemon and Phase-3 git writers). Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.languageNotes: Pure-Python stdlib arithmetic (no torch, no nn.Module inheritance); accepts torch tensors defensively via getattr/hasattr and coerces to a Python list before per-scalar EMA math.

nodes.name: ConditionedSafetyStore
nodes.summary: EMA-prototype conditioned safety predictor for SD-051 / MECH-304: learns which z_world states predict suffering absence via MECH-302 relief events (encoding pathway) and emits a sigmoid(cosine)-based safety_prediction scalar (expression pathway). Optional SD-066 centered mode subtracts a slow common-mode baseline before matching so a small cue residual can dominate under SD-008 z_world under-differentiation. MECH-094-gated: simulation ticks never advance the prototype.
nodes.languageNotes: Prototype + optional baseline held as plain Python lists updated in place; supports both raw-cosine and SD-066 centered-residue readouts under a single gain-adjusted sigmoid.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Configures the safety store: world_dim, EMA / decay / gain / threshold knobs, and the SD-066 centered-mode toggle plus its baseline_alpha. Initialises the prototype vector, the optional common-mode baseline, and internal counters (n_events, has_prototype).

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Waking-path tick: coerces the incoming z_world into a plain list, optionally advances the SD-066 common-mode baseline EMA (skipped in centered-mode when sim_mode is set), applies per-step L2 decay toward zero, and on a MECH-302 event tick blends the (centered or raw) z_world into the prototype via ema_alpha. Returns the current safety-prediction scalar via _query. Under sim_mode returns 0.0 with no state change (MECH-094).
nodes.languageNotes: Defensive tensor coercion (detach/squeeze/tolist) keeps the class torch-free while accepting torch inputs; L2 decay + EMA implemented as scalar list comprehensions.

nodes.name: _query
nodes.summary: Internal read: returns 0.0 when the prototype norm is below min_norm (no learned cue yet); otherwise computes cosine similarity between the query vector and the prototype and maps it through a scaled sigmoid (gain * cos) to produce the safety_prediction scalar in [0,1].

nodes.name: predict
nodes.summary: Read-only prediction API added 2026-07-15 for SD-059 / MECH-358: coerces z_world into a list, applies SD-066 centering when enabled (without mutating the baseline), and returns _query(...) as the safety signal fed into the escape-affordance bridge. Never advances prototype or baseline state.

nodes.name: RBFLayer.compute_local_density

nodes.name: RBFLayer.update_valence
nodes.summary: Updates the signed valence of an existing RBF center — used by ResidueField.update_valence to promote / demote residues after outcome resolution.

nodes.name: RBFLayer.evaluate_valence

nodes.summary: Constructs the ResidueField — instantiates the harm RBFLayer plus optional benefit (ARC-030/MECH-117) and safety (SD-052/066/067) RBFLayers, sets EWC anchoring state, and wires valence-priority thresholds.

nodes.name: ResidueField.ewc_penalty

nodes.name: ResidueField.evaluate
nodes.summary: Evaluates the harm residue field at a z_world query — thin wrapper delegating to the harm RBFLayer.forward pass.

nodes.name: ResidueField.evaluate_benefit
nodes.summary: ARC-030 / MECH-117 benefit-terrain read — evaluates the benefit RBFLayer at z_world; higher means closer to a previously-beneficial region (liking channel).

nodes.name: ResidueField.accumulate_benefit

nodes.name: ResidueField.compute_benefit_density
nodes.summary: SD-024 benefit-density readout — delegates to the benefit RBFLayer's compute_local_density so the DA-modulated allocation pathway can distinguish benefit-dense from benefit-sparse regions.

nodes.name: ResidueField.evaluate_safety
nodes.summary: SD-052 / SD-066 / SD-067 safety-terrain read — evaluates the safety RBFLayer at z_world; positive value means a previously-safe region, feeding hippocampal terrain scoring.

nodes.summary: Regression tests for reconcile_once's upsert_only mode confirming stale DB rows survive (safe under concurrent writers) while the legacy default-mode still deletes stale rows.

nodes.name: ConflictRecovery
nodes.summary: Tests the PHASE3_QUEUE_CONFLICT_RECOVERY self-heal path: fabricates a diverging origin edit + a local writer-authored ahead commit, then asserts the flag-on path resets, re-materialises, and lands the DB view while the flag-off path refuses and the foreign-commit rejection still holds.

nodes.name: NoSelfDeadlockOnFailedTick
nodes.summary: Failure-recovery tests using a failing pre-commit hook and a flaky-git monkeypatch to verify the writer leaves the working tree clean after a failed commit or failed post-write fetch and successfully recovers on the next tick.

nodes.name: OPERATOR_GUIDE.md
nodes.summary: Operator guide for the Phase-3 shadow coordination service, covering the Explorer coordination panel, mental model of writers and daemons, phased cutover from git-as-IPC to sync_daemon, and troubleshooting of writer wedges, telemetry drift, and daemon code drift incidents.
nodes.languageNotes: Long-form operational runbook with 24 sections spanning coordination panel semantics, phase transitions, and post-mortem-style incident notes with concrete queries and remediation commands.

nodes.name: actor_critic.py
nodes.summary: First-class actor-critic action-learning primitive (MECH-457): dorsal-striatal-analog actor with a Categorical over discrete actions plus optional plain, successor-feature, or distributional critic heads, architecturally distinct from lateral_pfc/OFC E3 bias-head REINFORCE readouts.
nodes.languageNotes: PyTorch nn.Module with dataclass step output; supports three critic modes (scalar value head, successor-feature via reward-weight vector, distributional value bins) selected by config flags.

nodes.name: ActorCriticStep
nodes.summary: Lightweight dataclass bundling one actor-critic decision step: sampled action index, log-probability, scalar value estimate, entropy, and diagnostic tensors (logits, successor phi/psi, distributional value logits).

nodes.name: ActorCriticPolicy
nodes.summary: Actor-critic policy nn.Module with shared MLP trunk, softmax policy head, and a switchable value critic (plain scalar / successor-feature reward-weighted / distributional two-hot bins); provides forward, critic loss, deterministic-or-stochastic action selection, and actor-parameter enumeration.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses torch.distributions.Categorical for stochastic sampling; ValueBins integration realises Dabney-2020-style distributional value estimation with HL-Gauss/two-hot projection.

nodes.name: phasic_surprise_burst.py
nodes.summary: SD-069 LC-NE phasic-surprise regulator that injects event-locked, exponentially-decaying temperature deltas onto the E3 softmax as the phasic complement to MECH-313's tonic noise-floor. Amended by SD-075 (2026-07-19) to add per-episode EMA baseline-continuity (carry vs reset) and accounting-only warmup gating so short-episode seeds no longer measure event count as a function of episode length.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure-arithmetic regulator (no nn.Module, no learned params); dataclass config + stateful class with EMA baseline, geometric envelope decay, and bit-identical OFF via master switch.

nodes.name: PhasicSurpriseBurstConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass holding the ten no-op-default knobs that parameterise PhasicSurpriseBurst: EMA decay for the surprise baseline, trigger ratio/floor, phasic temperature delta, envelope decay, minimum-temperature floor, excess saturation, SD-075 baseline_continuity ('carry'|'reset') and warmup_ticks accounting knobs.

nodes.name: PhasicSurpriseBurst
nodes.summary: Stateful phasic-surprise burst regulator: per-tick EMA baseline on a surprise signal (running_variance or instantaneous_pe), event-detection when surprise crosses trigger_ratio x baseline, geometric envelope decay driving a temperature delta on the E3 softmax. SD-075 amend adds carry/reset EMA-baseline-continuity across reset() and accounting-only warmup gating (n_events_converged vs n_events_prewarmup) so short-episode phasic experiments read against a converged baseline.

nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Pure-stdlib HTTP coordinator server (http.server + sqlite3) that serves as the fleet's central control plane: authenticates workers, arbitrates queue claims, ingests result manifests/heartbeats, and issues per-machine commands.
nodes.languageNotes: Zero-dependency design (ThreadingHTTPServer) chosen because the deploy target is a minimal Hetzner CX22 where every venv dep is a fragility source; bearer-token auth loaded from a JSON file, ASCII-only stdout for Windows cp1252 safety.

nodes.name: db.py
nodes.summary: SQLite persistence layer for the coordinator: schema migrations, atomic queue-claim UPDATE with heartbeat-aware staleness rules, phantom-completion classification, git-vs-coordinator divergence logging, heartbeat/status recording, and per-machine command channel.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-process-writer SQLite (WAL mode + BEGIN IMMEDIATE) uses the WHERE clause of a conditional UPDATE as the claim mutex, avoiding any external lock.

nodes.name: _read_writer_health
nodes.summary: Reads and returns the phase-3 writer health snapshot JSON from disk, returning an empty dict when absent or unreadable so /writer-health always responds.

nodes.name: _age_out_errors
nodes.summary: Filters writer-health error entries older than a cutoff timestamp so the exposed snapshot only shows recent failures.

nodes.name: auth_machine
nodes.summary: Parses an Authorization header, matches the bearer token against the tokens.json map, and returns the associated machine label (or None on failure).

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Binds the ThreadingHTTPServer to the configured host/port, initialises the SQLite database, and enters serve_forever.

nodes.name: Handler
nodes.summary: BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass implementing every coordinator endpoint: /health, /claim, /result, /heartbeat, /status, /command, /writer-health, /shadow/* -- with bearer-token auth, JSON body parsing, and delegation into db.py for state changes.

nodes.name: _migrate_experiments
nodes.summary: Additive schema migration that records WHY a queue row went terminal (removal_reason + result_outcome) so status='completed' rows can be distinguished between operator cancel, runner ERROR, scientific FAIL, and real completion.

nodes.name: _migrate_heartbeats
nodes.summary: Adds heartbeat and status tables plus shutdown-notice tracking so lifecycle_state can classify machines as live vs stale vs planned-down.

nodes.name: _migrate_commands
nodes.summary: Creates the per-machine command channel table (kind, args_json, ack/result) used by /command endpoints for pause/resume/stop/kick semantics.

nodes.name: upsert_experiment
nodes.summary: Inserts or updates a queue row from a queue.json item, preserving an active claim across snapshots and updating machine_affinity + priority in place.

nodes.name: _parse_utc
nodes.summary: Best-effort UTC datetime parser accepting the coordinator's ISO-8601-Z serialization, returning None on any malformation.

nodes.name: _has_fresh_owner_heartbeat
nodes.summary: Returns True when the claim's owning machine posted a heartbeat within the fresh-window, blocking a stale-based recovery of a still-live worker.

nodes.name: try_claim
nodes.summary: Atomic conditional UPDATE that assigns queue_id to a machine iff the row is currently unclaimed or held by a recoverable stale owner; the WHERE clause is the mutex.

nodes.name: evaluate_claim
nodes.summary: Non-mutating version of try_claim used by the shadow-mode check to compare coordinator verdicts against the git-based claim outcome.

nodes.name: apply_git_outcome
nodes.summary: In Phase 1 / Phase 2 shadow modes, applies the git-observed claim verdict (accept/reject/recover) to the DB row so the mirror stays consistent with git-as-authority.

nodes.name: release_claim
nodes.summary: Clears a claim held by a specific machine, guarding against releasing a rival's claim; used on clean shutdown and stale recovery.

nodes.name: mark_queue_removed
nodes.summary: Marks a queue row terminal with a removal_reason (removed/cancelled/error/fail/superseded) so the phantom-completion classifier can tell them apart.

nodes.name: claim_verdicts_diverge
nodes.summary: Detects when the git-based claim verdict disagrees with the coordinator's evaluate_claim (with an is_explained_divergence carve-out for benign heartbeat-freshness edges).

nodes.name: divergence_stats
nodes.summary: Aggregates counts and per-machine breakdowns of claim verdict divergences for the /divergence endpoint operator view.

nodes.name: record_result
nodes.summary: Persists the outcome and manifest bytes for a completed run so phase3_git_writer can pick it up and commit it into REE_assembly.

nodes.name: upsert_heartbeat
nodes.summary: Upserts a machine's latest heartbeat (state, current_exq, progress) into the heartbeats table with monotonic seq, plus a state-history append-only row for phase3 heartbeat-writer change detection.

nodes.name: record_status_payload
nodes.summary: Persists an opaque JSON status payload (runner_status) so the phase3 writer can materialise the runner_status/*.json git files.

nodes.name: record_shutdown_notice
nodes.summary: Records a planned-down notice so the cloud-scaler and lifecycle classifier can distinguish deliberate shutdowns from unresponsive workers.

nodes.name: lifecycle_state
nodes.summary: Classifies a machine as live/stale/planned-down/never-seen from the heartbeat timestamp and any recent shutdown_notice; the primary input to /machines UI freshness.

nodes.name: insert_command
nodes.summary: Enqueues a per-machine command (pause/resume/stop/force_stop/kick/release_claim) to be delivered on the next /command GET from that worker.

nodes.name: ack_command
nodes.summary: Marks a delivered command acknowledged with a result_status and note, arming the operator dashboard's per-command feedback UI.

nodes.name: get_queue_status
nodes.summary: Reads a queue row (status + removal_reason + claim + result_outcome) for a queue_id, used by phase3 writers to detect phantom completions and by the queue materialiser.

nodes.name: sync_daemon.py
nodes.summary: Multi-mode sync daemon that reconciles the coordinator SQLite DB with the git-authoritative experiment queue and, in Phase 3, becomes the sole git writer for evidence manifests, queue snapshots, and heartbeats -- with strict guards against autostash-driven silent reverts of session work.
nodes.languageNotes: Three-phase gating (shadow / coordinator / authoritative) selected by SYNC_MODE + --i-understand-phase3; the writer path never rebase-autostashes to avoid silently reverting operators' uncommitted evidence edits (the entire raison d'etre of the daemon).

nodes.name: reconcile_once
nodes.summary: Reconciles the coordinator DB mirror against the git-authoritative experiment_queue.json in one pass -- upserts, removals, and (outside upsert-only mode) claim-authority translation of git verdicts into DB state.

nodes.name: _validate_abs_repo_path
nodes.summary: Validates a runtime env var that names an absolute repo path, refusing traversal or non-existent targets so a misconfigured writer refuses to run rather than corrupt a random tree.

nodes.name: _validate_repo_relpath
nodes.summary: Validates that a relative path lives inside the repo and does not traverse; used by every path-taking env knob for the phase3 writers.

nodes.name: _validate_float
nodes.summary: Bounded-range float validator used for phase3 writer tuning knobs (backoffs, intervals) so a fat-fingered env var falls back to a safe default rather than a wedge.

nodes.name: _validate_bool
nodes.summary: Bool validator for phase3 feature gates that treats unknown/mistyped values as the safe default and logs the fallback.

nodes.name: _record_writer_commit
nodes.summary: Records a successful writer commit into the in-memory writer-health snapshot: last_commit_at, subject, per-writer counters, and origin sync state.

nodes.name: _bootstrap_writer_health_from_git
nodes.summary: On daemon start, replays recent git log for the phase3 writer commit prefixes to seed writer-health with last_commit_at values, so /writer-health is meaningful before the first tick lands.

nodes.name: _extract_heartbeat_machine_state
nodes.summary: Extracts the machine-state tuple (state, current_exq, progress, extras) used by the phase3 heartbeat writer's change-detection debounce.

nodes.name: _phase3_heartbeat_compute_changes
nodes.summary: Computes the delta between the last-committed heartbeat state and current DB state, filtering out uninteresting drifts (progress bumps between state changes) so the writer commits on state changes only, not every tick.

nodes.name: _phase3_heartbeat_phrase
nodes.summary: Renders a per-machine heartbeat change into a short human-readable phrase used in the commit subject line for the phase3-heartbeats: writer.

nodes.name: _revert_target_to_head
nodes.summary: Restores a single dirty tracked path back to its HEAD content and re-adds it to the index; used to revert stray writer-target dirt before every writer tick.

nodes.name: _maybe_revert_exclusive_telemetry_dirt
nodes.summary: When only heartbeat/status paths are dirty (no session evidence in flight), reverts them so a phase3 writer tick can proceed instead of refusing on the dirty tree.

nodes.name: _restore_derived_path
nodes.summary: Materialises a HEAD/index-only path (missing from the working tree, typically after a mixed reset) back onto disk so the writers do not see phantom deletions.

nodes.name: _active_claim_blocks_writer
nodes.summary: Reads TASK_CLAIMS.json and refuses a writer tick when an active session claim covers any of the writer's target paths -- the primary defense against the autostash-driven silent revert failure class.

nodes.name: _check_ahead_writer_authored
nodes.summary: Checks whether the local branch is ahead of origin only by writer-authored commit prefixes, so a phase3 writer refuses to force-rebase over an operator commit.

nodes.name: _sync_to_origin
nodes.summary: Fetches origin and reconciles local writer commits: fast-forwards, rebases writer-authored commits onto refreshed origin, or (for the queue writer only, gated by PHASE3_QUEUE_CONFLICT_RECOVERY) hard-resets and re-materialises from DB on conflict.

nodes.name: _load_runpack_builder
nodes.summary: Late-imports the ree-v3 runpack builder (evidence per-run pack) so the daemon does not carry a hard import dependency on the substrate repo.

nodes.name: _materialize_runpacks
nodes.summary: Materialises evidence per-run manifest/metrics/summary packs from the DB result payload into REE_assembly/evidence/experiments/runs/<run_id>/ before the writer commits them.

nodes.name: _materialize_sidefiles
nodes.summary: Materialises any per-run sidefiles the runner uploaded via the spool (plots, logs) alongside the manifest so a single writer commit lands the whole run pack.

nodes.name: phase3_git_writer
nodes.summary: Sole git writer for evidence manifests in REE_assembly: pulls the spool from the coordinator DB + disk, materialises runpacks and sidefiles, commits with the phase3: prefix, and pushes -- guarded by the active-claim check and the exclusive-telemetry revert.

nodes.name: _canonicalise_queue_item
nodes.summary: Normalises a DB-materialised queue item's field order and defaults so the emitted experiment_queue.json is stable across writer restarts.

nodes.name: _materialise_queue_from_db
nodes.summary: Renders experiment_queue.json from the DB experiments table (active + claimed rows only), used both by the queue writer and by the queue-conflict recovery path.

nodes.name: _warn_on_terminal_drops_without_results
nodes.summary: Emits a warning (never a block) when a queue row goes terminal without a corresponding result row -- the phantom-completion detector at the writer boundary.

nodes.name: phase3_queue_writer
nodes.summary: Sole git writer for ree-v3/experiment_queue.json: computes the target queue from the DB, writes atomically, commits with phase3-queue:, and self-heals rebase conflicts by resetting to origin and re-materialising when PHASE3_QUEUE_CONFLICT_RECOVERY is set.

nodes.name: _atomic_write_text
nodes.summary: Writes text to a temp file, fsyncs, and renames -- used for every writer-produced file so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated queue or heartbeat file.

nodes.name: _safe_machine_filename
nodes.summary: Sanitises a machine label into a filesystem-safe filename for the per-machine runner_heartbeats/*.json and runner_status/*.json artifacts.

nodes.name: phase3_heartbeat_writer
nodes.summary: Sole git writer for runner_heartbeats/*.json and runner_status/*.json: commits on state changes only (retired the 30-min forced liveness tick 2026-06-23) to cap git-history bloat, using compute_changes for debouncing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses SYNC_MODE + --i-understand-phase3, wires up the three writers, and enters the reconcile/writer loop.

nodes.name: agent.py
nodes.summary: REE-V3 agent core (10425 lines) integrating all architectural components: LatentStack (z_self/z_world split), E1/E2/E3 predictor stack, HippocampalModule, ResidueField, cingulate/PFC/amygdala regulators, sleep loop, and the multi-rate heartbeat clock. Defines REEAgent (nn.Module) plus AgentState dataclass and diagnostic helpers used across the substrate.
nodes.languageNotes: Monolithic 10K-line orchestrator class with 91 methods; imports 43 project-internal modules from every ree_core subsystem. Uses PyTorch nn.Module inheritance; heavily depends on optional feature flags on REEConfig for gated wiring.

nodes.name: candidate_support_preflight
nodes.summary: Diagnostic-only preflight that computes first-action support metrics (class counts, entropy, forced-bias summaries) over a candidate trajectory set. Callers decide whether the interpretation is well-posed based on the returned status flag.

nodes.name: _resolve_chunk_deliberation_horizon
nodes.summary: Sentinel-defaulted resolver returning the MECH-323 chunk-ceiling deliberation horizon: 0 mirrors HippocampalConfig.horizon (fallback 10), positive values are explicit experimental overrides honoured verbatim.

nodes.name: AgentState
nodes.summary: Dataclass snapshot of the complete REE-V3 agent state at one timestep: latent state, precision, running variance, step count, harm accumulator, commitment/beta flags, E3 tick rate, and optional serotonergic state.

nodes.name: REEAgent
nodes.summary: Central Reflective-Ethical Engine agent (nn.Module, 91 methods, ~10K lines) that composes every V3 subsystem: LatentStack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal proposer, residue field, cingulate/PFC/amygdala regulators, sleep loop, heartbeat clock, and all learned/pure-arithmetic policy heads. Owns sense-select-act-update-residue-replay-offline loop and gates dozens of optional substrates via REEConfig feature flags.
nodes.languageNotes: Deeply flag-driven: ~80% of __init__ conditionally builds optional substrates from getattr() fallbacks on REEConfig; select_action alone is ~3000 lines composing 12+ modulatory channels.

nodes.name: __init__
nodes.summary: Massive constructor (2484 lines) that instantiates the full V3 substrate: latent encoders, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal + residue modules, all cingulate/PFC/amygdala/policy regulators, sleep loop, heartbeat clock, and dozens of optional feature-flagged levers. Wires cross-module dependencies and enforces loud preconditions for the ~50 substrate cluster flags.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Per-episode reset that clears the multi-rate clock, beta gate, E3 selector state, residue accumulators, and every optional regulator (BLA/CeA, PAG, blocked-agency, avoidance gate, escape bridge, closure operator, chunk facades, natural-commit hold, etc.). Preserves cross-episode learned state (super-ordinal anchors, ghost bank, learned selection weights).

nodes.name: _update_blocked_agency
nodes.summary: Runs the MECH-353 blocked-agency comparator: uses SD-029 world-forward and motor-agency comparators to detect predicted-but-blocked actions, updates z_block affect stream, and stages the assert/decommit signals consumed later in select_action.

nodes.name: _update_scientist_attribution
nodes.summary: Runs the MECH-276 scientist-attribution counterfactual comparators (SD-031 world, ARC-033 harm-s) on waking transitions and buffers counterfactual-backed attributions into ScientistAttributionBuffer as feedstock for the MECH-275 sleep-phase Bayesian aggregator.

nodes.name: sense
nodes.summary: Primary perception entry point (~940 lines) that encodes body/world observations into the split latent state, runs SD-019a z_harm_un EMA + MECH-219 suffering accumulator, invokes the SD-036 GABAergic decay, ticks BLA/CeA/AIC amygdala-analog regulators, updates per-stream V_s, event segmenter, invalidation trigger, anchor set, TPJ comparator, and dozens of downstream sensory-side substrates.

nodes.name: _e1_tick
nodes.summary: Per-tick E1 predictor update: runs E1DeepPredictor.predict_long_horizon (with optional MECH-269b V_s gating and SD-016 cue extraction), caches schema-salience readouts, updates the MECH-089 theta buffer, and observes the multi-content theta packet (MECH-294) when enabled.

nodes.name: _e3_tick
nodes.summary: Per-tick E3 update: reads the theta-cycle summary, runs the hippocampal proposer with optional MECH-293 ghost probes, seals the MECH-294 multi-content packet, applies MECH-105 hippocampal completion coupling to the beta gate, and triggers MECH-290 backward credit sweep on release.

nodes.name: generate_trajectories
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper generating CEM candidate trajectories via the HippocampalModule proposer, threading E1 prior context and the current z_goal (when active) for MECH-293 ghost-goal probe seeding.

nodes.name: select_action
nodes.summary: Massive selection routine (~3000 lines) composing every score-bias channel (dACC, lateral-PFC, OFC, MECH-295 liking bridge, MECH-314 curiosity, MECH-320 vigor, MECH-341 diversity, MECH-353 assert, escape/avoidance biases, gated policy, tonic vigor, MECH-451 finer, MECH-140 disinhibition, MECH-450 W_lat settling, MECH-448 F-eligibility, MECH-449 Go/No-Go, learned channel gating, ARC-110 loop segregation, ARC-108 x ARC-110 cross-loop, MECH-091 urgency, MECH-342 maintenance release, MECH-450 recurrent settling, rung-6 natural-commit release, SD-034 closure operator, MECH-090 beta gate). Central F-dominance conversion-ceiling battleground.

nodes.name: notify_env_completion
nodes.summary: Public seam letting the environment (or experiment harness) route a transition_type=='sequence_complete' event into the SD-034 ClosureOperator.emit_closure path, delivering the Leg-A env-completion hook the commitment-closure-control-plane amend adds.

nodes.name: note_chunk_replay_sequence
nodes.summary: MECH-322 waking replay-origin carve-out into the ARC-071 policy-chunking accumulator: records an internally-generated action sequence with hypothesis_tag=True and the accompanying value/replay-origin audit metadata for the ChunkedPrimitive.

nodes.name: act
nodes.summary: High-level convenience wrapper composing sense() + select_action() into a single call returning (action_tensor, AgentState snapshot). Manages optional harm-stream inputs and per-tick state bookkeeping.

nodes.name: update_residue
nodes.summary: Post-step residue update integrating MECH-094-gated world-delta accumulation, MECH-205 surprise-gated valence writes, MECH-302 relief comparator, SD-051/052 safety store/terrain, SD-024 benefit-terrain live producer, MECH-091 urgency interrupt, JOB-2 habenula negative-RPE de-commit, and MECH-353 blocked-agency accumulation.

nodes.name: compute_prediction_loss
nodes.summary: Computes the E1 predictive-coding loss (MSE over predicted vs observed z-stream) plus the SD-016 ContextMemory diversification auxiliary loss when enabled. Primary E1 training objective.

nodes.name: compute_event_contrastive_loss
nodes.summary: SD-009 event-contrastive cross-entropy auxiliary loss on the z_world encoder using event-type labels, forcing z_world to represent hazard-vs-empty distinctions beyond reconstruction invariance.

nodes.name: compute_resource_proximity_loss
nodes.summary: SD-018 resource-proximity MSE auxiliary loss on the z_world encoder using max(resource_field_view) as the sigmoid target, keeping z_world representationally sensitive to resource proximity.

nodes.name: compute_resource_encoder_loss
nodes.summary: SD-015 z_resource encoder auxiliary loss: MSE of resource_prox_pred_r against proximity targets, gradient flows through the location-invariant ResourceEncoder that seeds z_goal in MECH-112/117 pathways.

nodes.name: compute_resource_identity_loss
nodes.summary: SD-049 Phase-2 hybrid identity-aware auxiliary loss: cross-entropy on the ResourceEncoder classifier head against obs_dict['sd049_consumed_type_tag_this_tick'], shaping z_resource identity discriminability.

nodes.name: compute_harm_nonredundancy_loss
nodes.summary: SD-019 auxiliary loss penalising cosine similarity between projected z_harm_s and z_harm_a streams, keeping sensory-discriminative and affective harm representations functionally non-overlapping under ARC-016 precision scaling.

nodes.name: compute_harm_accum_loss
nodes.summary: SD-011 second-source auxiliary loss on the AffectiveHarmEncoder harm_accum_head predicting the accumulated-harm scalar (optionally surprise-PE weighted under SD-020) so z_harm_a integrates temporal harm history.

nodes.name: update_z_goal
nodes.summary: Core goal-pipeline update (269 lines): applies SD-012 sustained-drive EMA, SD-037 broadcast override amplification, MECH-295 liking-bridge write, MECH-307 predicted-location schema pulse, SD-057 IncentiveTokenBank per-object binding, MECH-189 super-ordinal goal anchors write/read, SD-024 benefit-terrain live producer, MECH-347 cue-recall wanting hook, and the GoalState.update firing gate.

nodes.name: cue_recall_wanting
nodes.summary: SD-057 L6 cue-recall primitive: retrieves the IncentiveTokenBank token for a perceived resource type, computes drive-specific wanting amplitude, and pulls z_goal toward the stored object embedding via GoalState.cue_pull.

nodes.name: update_schema_wanting
nodes.summary: MECH-216 predictive-wanting integrator: reads the cached E1 schema salience, gates by drive level, and writes VALENCE_WANTING to the ResidueField at the current z_world (optionally amplifying z_beta arousal under MECH-307).

nodes.name: run_sws_schema_pass
nodes.summary: SD-017 SWS-analog offline pass: samples diverse z_world prototypes from the world-experience buffer, constructs [z_self, z_world] E1 inputs, writes to ContextMemory bypassing the offline gate, applies MECH-120 SHY normalisation, and reports slot-diversity metrics.

nodes.name: run_rem_attribution_pass
nodes.summary: SD-017 REM-analog offline pass: replays recent theta-buffer content via HippocampalModule.replay and diverse_replay, evaluates residue terrain without accumulating new residue (hypothesis_tag=True per MECH-094), and applies MECH-204 precision recalibration when enabled.

nodes.name: run_sleep_cycle
nodes.summary: Convenience method running SWS then REM in sequence with correct mode transitions (enter_sws_mode -> run_sws_schema_pass -> exit_sleep_mode -> enter_rem_mode -> run_rem_attribution_pass -> exit_sleep_mode) and merging metrics for consumers bypassing the SleepLoopManager.

nodes.name: _assemble_control_vector
nodes.summary: Read-only telemetry assembler (169 lines) that builds the four-signal ControlVector diagnostic: V_outcome / C_effort / C_time / G_vigor per-tick decomposition surfaced on _last_control_vector for downstream reporting. Exposes the ARC-068-vs-MECH-320 collapse structurally.

nodes.name: stack.py
nodes.summary: V3 Latent Stack (L-space) implementing SD-005: split-encoder architecture producing z_self, z_world, z_beta, z_theta, z_delta with harm-stream (z_harm, z_harm_a) and resource encoders, plus reafference correction and iterative-inference settling. Central hub feeding E1/E2/E3, hippocampal, and residue-field modules.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains 15 nn.Module classes spanning encoders, forward models, adversarial split heads, and a monolithic LatentStack (575 lines) that orchestrates encode/predict/precision-modulation with SD-007 reafference, SD-008 alpha_world smoothing, and DR-13 self-recurrence hooks.

nodes.name: ReafferencePredictor
nodes.summary: SD-007/MECH-098/MECH-101 perspective-shift correction: predicts the z_world change caused purely by self-motion (locomotion) so exteroceptive latents can be corrected for reafference before downstream consumers read them.

nodes.name: HarmEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-010 sensory-discriminative (A-delta analog) harm encoder mapping harm_obs to z_harm; trained on hazard-proximity supervision to feed E3 harm evaluation and E2_harm_s forward modeling.

nodes.name: AffectiveHarmEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-011 affective (C-fiber analog) harm encoder producing z_harm_a with optional harm_history input and auxiliary accumulated-harm regression head; drives urgency, MECH-219 suffering integration, and dACC modulation.

nodes.name: ResourceEncoder
nodes.summary: SD-015 z_resource encoder producing location-invariant resource identity embedding plus SD-018 proximity auxiliary head; optional SD-049 Phase 2 identity classifier for hybrid discriminative training.

nodes.name: HarmForwardModel
nodes.summary: Baseline forward model predicting next-step z_harm from current z_harm and action; used by SD-003 counterfactual pipeline and ARC-033 E2_harm_s successors.

nodes.name: HarmForwardTrunk
nodes.summary: ARC-058 shared-substrate harm forward trunk: modality-independent unsigned PE substrate combined with per-modality signed HarmForwardHead readouts for z_harm_s and z_harm_a streams.

nodes.name: HarmForwardHead
nodes.summary: Per-modality signed prediction head consuming HarmForwardTrunk shared features; instantiates ARC-058 stream-specific readouts (z_harm_s or z_harm_a).

nodes.name: ResidualHarmForward
nodes.summary: Residual-delta forward model preventing identity collapse on autocorrelated z_harm signals; underpins SD-031 E2WorldForward and ARC-033 E2HarmSForward wrappers via delta-prediction rather than direct next-state output.

nodes.name: HarmBridge
nodes.summary: Deprecated bridge attempting z_world->z_harm mapping (bridge_r2=0 confirmed architectural per EXQ-093/094); retained for legacy compatibility but superseded by direct harm-stream comparators.

nodes.name: AdversarialSplitHead
nodes.summary: Gradient-reversal adversarial head enforcing separation between z_self and z_world (or harm sub-streams) so encoders cannot cross-leak information, supporting the SD-005 split invariant.

nodes.name: LatentState

tour.title: Substrate God-Class: The Agent Core
tour.description: Start at ree_core/agent.py -- the 10k-line REEAgent that integrates every V3 module (latent stack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal, residue, cingulate, PFC, regulators). It is the highest fan-out node in the graph (43 outgoing imports), which is why we anchor the tour here rather than at a lightweight main.py: agent.py IS the substrate's runtime. The ree_core package marker is included so you can see where the boundary between substrate and the rest of the world sits.
tour.languageLesson: The god-class is a deliberate architectural choice here, not a smell: V3's contract is that every cognitive concern -- self/world separation, harm modelling, motivational persistence -- must affect the state from which the agent generates and commits to actions. Distributing that across many owners would let those concerns be added as post-hoc scores or safety filters, which is what the architecture explicitly refuses.

tour.title: Configuration Hub and the Training World
tour.description: REEConfig in ree_core/utils/config.py is the single umbrella that pins every subsystem's dataclass knobs (latent stack, predictors, hippocampal, residue, heartbeat, environment). It has fan-in 10 -- almost every experiment reads from it. The causal_grid_world environment supplies the observations agent.py steps against: a 2D grid where body_state and world_state channels are already split at the sensor level, matching the SD-005 z_self / z_world commitment the latent stack encodes downstream.

tour.title: Latent Stack -- L-space and the SD-005 Split
tour.description: The latent stack encodes each observation into the (z_self, z_world, z_beta, z_theta, z_delta) tuple, plus the harm streams (z_harm, z_harm_a) and resource encoders. This is the design commitment referenced everywhere else: the agent's self-model and world-model are separate at the representational level, not fused into a single latent. Every predictor and every regulator downstream reads from this split; break it and the rest of the substrate stops meaning what it claims to mean.

tour.title: The E1 -> E2 -> E3 Prediction Cascade
tour.description: E1 is the slow LSTM-based world model over the concatenated latent; E2 is the fast forward model of world-state consequences plus a harm-affective forward model that supplies dACC's control-demand signal; E3 is the trajectory selector that scores candidate actions with J(zeta) = F + lambda*M + rho*Phi_R. This cascade is where the architectural commitment from Step 3 becomes computable: each candidate action is scored against a self-model, a world-model, and an anticipated harm signal, before any commitment is made.

tour.title: Hippocampal Module and the Residue Field
tour.description: The hippocampal module runs a CEM search over the action-object space O to generate value-flat proposals for E3, replays during quiescent heartbeats, and maintains anchors and event segments. The ResidueField accumulates RBF-based harm/benefit/safety over z_world with per-center bandwidth (SD-024) and EWC anchoring -- so the consequences of earlier actions are durable state the agent's next decision must integrate over, not scores that decay to zero on the next tick.

tour.title: Persistent Goal Representation and Action-Selection
tour.description: goal.py defines z_goal_latent -- the persistent super-ordinal goal memory, incentive token bank, and per-agent goal state that survives across ticks. GatedPolicy is the ARC-062 weak-reading rule-apprehension layer: two symmetry-broken scoring heads plus a learned context discriminator gate between them, giving E3 something more principled to select over than a single softmax. Together they answer 'what is the agent trying to do, and how does it pick a candidate that serves that intention'.

tour.title: Cingulate Salience Network and PFC Analogues
tour.description: SalienceCoordinator (SD-032a) aggregates the dACC bundle plus interoceptive/attention/autonomic signals into a soft operating-mode probability vector and drives MECH-259 mode-switch decisions. LateralPFC-analog (SD-033a) is the mid-lateral rule/goal substrate whose EMA rule_state is gate-modulated by salience write-gates. per_axis_drive is the SD-049 helper that routes the drive vector into these consumers -- a small but load-bearing shared accessor.

tour.title: Regulators: Broadcast Override and Invalidation Triggers
tour.description: The regulators layer holds cross-cutting guardrails that override the normal candidate-scoring flow when the substrate needs to. BroadcastOverride (SD-037) is an orexin analog: a sigmoid recruitment on drive_level + sustained-threat magnitude that produces a scalar [0,1] override signal. InvalidationTrigger (MECH-287) subscribes to MECH-288 boundary events and re-emits them as graded BroadcastEvents so anchor sets reset and staleness consumers wake up -- the mechanism that lets the agent notice its world has changed under it.

tour.title: Blocked-Agency Signal and Counterfactual Attribution
tour.description: blocked_agency.py derives z_block, the control-failure signal that rises when an intended action repeatedly fails against an external constraint while goal and capacity remain intact -- the substrate's readout that the agent is being blocked rather than merely failing. ScientistAttributionBuffer (MECH-276) records only counterfactually-backed credit attributions during waking, filtering out mere correlational associations before they can feed the sleep-phase Bayesian aggregator in the next step.

tour.title: Sleep Loop and Offline Consolidation
tour.description: SleepLoopManager (SD-017) drives the deterministic K-episode entry into the sleep cycle: WAKING -> SWS -> PHASE_SWITCH -> REM -> WRITEBACK. This is where the attribution buffer from Step 9 is aggregated, the hippocampal replay in Step 5 is consumed, and consolidated updates are written back to E1/E2. Sleep here is not a housekeeping detail -- it is where 'offline integration' from the README's list of substrate prerequisites actually happens.

tour.title: Coordination Plane: The Phase-3 Plan-of-Record
tour.description: The coordinator is a separate concern from the substrate: it is the fleet-side control plane that arbitrates queue claims, ingests result manifests from cloud workers, and (in Phase 3) becomes the sole git writer for coordination data. PLAN.md is the rationale + target end-state; PHASE3_CUTOVER.md is the plan-of-record for the result-write cutover including env knobs, preconditions, cutover procedure, and rollback. Reading these before the code makes the writer-vs-runner race constraints they encode legible.
tour.languageLesson: A plan-of-record markdown pairs a rationale with an inspectable rollout: 'what we are cutting over, what the preconditions are, what the operator does, what the rollback is'. Treat it as executable text -- changes to the code plane must land in the plan first, or the plan stops being a plan and becomes stale documentation.

tour.title: Coordinator HTTP Surface and SQLite Persistence
tour.description: coordinator/app.py is a pure-stdlib http.server + sqlite3 HTTP surface (no framework dependency, so the hub can run it under systemd with no venv drift) that authenticates workers, arbitrates /claim, and receives POST /result / POST /heartbeat. coordinator/db.py is where the interesting logic lives: schema migrations, atomic queue-claim UPDATEs with heartbeat-aware staleness rules, phantom-completion classification, and git-vs-coordinator reconciliation. db.py has fan-in 14, the highest in the whole graph -- almost every coordinator module depends on it.

tour.title: Schema, Spool, and the Sole Git Writer
tour.description: schema.sql defines the five coordinator tables -- experiments, results, heartbeats, commands, claim_log -- that back the persistence layer from Step 12. manifest_spool.py persists POST /result bytes to disk keyed on run_id so a later git commit is race-free. sync_daemon.py is the payoff: in Phase 3 it is the SOLE git writer for coordination data (evidence manifests, queue snapshot, heartbeats), which is what closes the multi-writer race that used to silently corrupt shared JSON files under concurrent worker load.
tour.languageLesson: SQL schema doubles as a coordination contract: each table pins the shape of one type of fleet event (a queue entry, a result, a heartbeat, a command, a claim). Migrations must be additive and ordered -- the sync_daemon reads these tables as truth, so a shape change without a migration would silently break every downstream git commit.

tour.title: Operator Runbook
tour.description: OPERATOR_GUIDE.md is the last stop: the Explorer coordination panel's mental model, the phased cutover from git-as-IPC to sync_daemon-as-writer, and the day-to-day playbook for the hub. Read it after the code because the runbook's decisions -- when to hold a writer, when to reconcile, when to fail -- only make sense once you have seen the schema, the spool, and the sync_daemon they operate on.
